semanticDecisions: both sides are read through String.getChars into two transient 256-unit windows; an M3 side copies from its owner in bulk, a flat side from its value array; the windows are scratch, never a shadow

the case rule follows the coders exactly as the stock single-coder paths do: per-unit rule when either side is Latin-1, code-point rule when both are UTF-16; results are byte-identical to two flat Strings, which the previous mixed paths (code-point rule for every pair) were not in the exotic coder/surrogate mixes
below 16 units the direct unit loop stays: two window copies cost more than sixteen dispatches (bench 8 vs 32 units)
factsIfPrepared(begin, end) never prepares anything; the ASCII fold gate over a prepared sub-range is sound by the same argument as the whole-owner gate (equal fold hashes are never rejected)
no new allocation on the short paths; the window allocation on long paths replaces N owner dispatches and is accepted as the A8 scan accepted its window
